# V1 Google OAuth verification resubmission

Project: `mailloop-510915` (number `842074495814`). Production: https://mailloop.in.

This guide concerns the send-only `main` release. Do not merge another branch to
prepare verification. Approval is Google's decision; a policy update alone does
not address the requested demo and reviewer access.

## Current implementation and remaining checks

- `src/auth.ts` requests only `openid email profile` and
  `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.send`.
- Gmail operations send individual messages using `users.messages.send`.
  There is no inbox reading, Gmail deletion, or automatic reply detection.
- The public privacy policy names Vercel, Neon, Vercel Blob, Inngest, Google,
  and selected recipients, explains the data each handles, and describes
  HTTPS, AES-256-GCM refresh-token encryption, server-side credential handling,
  authenticated account access, private PDFs, and limited operational records.
- Sign-in uses Google only. V1 has no separate local password, app invitation,
  subscription purchase, or credit-card requirement. Keep authentication enabled.
- Verify the production OAuth client belongs to this project and the actual
  hosting/database/storage providers match the policy before resubmitting.
  The Cloud Console configuration cannot be inferred from repository code.

The privacy disclosures were already present on the live site when checked on
October 31, 2026. This follow-up adds direct section links. Deploy `main` if those
links are not yet present in production; no migration or new environment variable
is required for this follow-up.

## Cloud Console and live access

1. Select `mailloop-510915` in Google Auth Platform.
2. In Branding, check the app identity, support contact, verified domain,
   homepage `https://mailloop.in/`, and privacy URL
   `https://mailloop.in/privacy`.
3. In Data Access and the verification request, retain only identity permissions
   and `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.send`. Remove any old read,
   modify, metadata, compose, or full-mailbox scopes from this submission.
   Explain the change if the previous submission included broader permissions.
4. Confirm the web OAuth client's authorized callback includes
   `https://mailloop.in/api/auth/callback/google`.
5. Check Audience/publishing status and any user-cap restriction. If access is
   limited to test users, obtain the reviewer's Google account address and add
   that exact address. Do not mistake the verification team's reply address for
   the account they will use to sign in. Resolve blocked access before replying.
6. Test the full flow below with a Google account and recipient addresses you
   control. Confirm live sending and the Inngest worker actually work.

If a reviewer needs credentials beyond Google sign-in, request their reviewer
account address for authorization or arrange a dedicated test account through
the verification thread. Never send personal account credentials or save any
test credentials in this repository. Do not add an authentication bypass.

## Recording the replacement demo

Use a real screen recording of the deployed app in English with readable text.
Keep the browser address bar visible, including the OAuth client ID during
authorization. Narration or captions should explain each step. Record all
scope-dependent user features, including personalized batch sends and an
explicitly selected resume attachment; do not substitute a promotional video.

Before recording, use a dedicated account you control and revoke its existing
Mailloop connection at https://myaccount.google.com/connections, then sign out
of Mailloop. This ensures old grants do not hide permissions or retain previous
mailbox-read access. Prepare a small, non-sensitive PDF and two controlled
recipient inboxes. Do not show passwords, tokens, or unrelated personal email.

1. Open the homepage, explain Mailloop's purpose, and show the public privacy
   policy, including the data-sharing and data-protection sections.
2. Click **Get started with Google**, choose the demo account, and show the
   complete Google sign-in and consent process. Expand **Show all services**
   and any permission details when offered. Leave every requested permission
   readable. Grant Gmail sending permission. If old read/modify permissions
   appear, stop and resolve the deployed client/scope mismatch first.
3. Show **Settings** with the signed-in address and Gmail sending enabled.
   Explain that identity permissions create the user's account and Gmail
   permission sends approved emails from that account. Click **Reconnect Gmail**
   and demonstrate that consent path too, expanding any permission details,
   then return to Settings.
4. Upload the demo PDF in **Settings**. In **Contacts**, add two addresses you
   control, with distinct names and a job role for each. Company is optional.
5. In **Templates**, save a named template with a unique subject, such as
   `Mailloop verification demo`, and body:

   ```text
   Hi {{name}},

   This is a controlled demonstration of Mailloop for the {{role}} role.
   Please find the selected demo PDF attached.
   ```

6. Open **Compose**, choose the saved template, select both recipients, confirm
   each role is filled, inspect each **Personal Preview**, and enable
   **Attach Resume**. Explain that each recipient gets a separate email.
7. Click **Send to 2 recipients** once. Show sending progress and **History**
   until both messages show **Sent**. Explain that this means Gmail accepted
   them, rather than proof of inbox delivery.
8. Open **Gmail → Sent** for the SAME sender account. Search the unique subject
   if necessary. Open both emails (expand the individual messages if Gmail
   groups them). Show sender, each single recipient, personalized body, and PDF
   attachment. Show there are no CC/BCC batch recipients. This is the required
   evidence of the change in the source Google account.
9. Explain that replies are checked in Gmail, and Mailloop does not read or
   delete mailbox messages. Deleting Mailloop history only deletes app records.
   No Gmail deletion demonstration is needed for this send-only release.

Upload the complete recording as an accessible unlisted YouTube video and test
the link while signed out. Keep the video available throughout review.

## Scope justification for the submission

> Mailloop is a standalone web app that sends user-approved, personalized job
> outreach emails from the user's own Gmail account. We use openid, email, and
> profile to authenticate the user and identify their account and sender name.
> We use https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.send with Gmail
> users.messages.send to send a separate message to each selected recipient,
> including a resume PDF only when the user explicitly selects it. This is the
> narrowest Gmail scope supporting this sending feature in our standalone web
> app. Identity-only scopes cannot send email; Gmail add-on scopes are for
> add-on interactions and do not support this standalone workflow. We do not
> request mailbox read, modify, compose/draft management, or deletion access.
> Replies are checked directly by the user in Gmail. Offline access supports
> processing the user's approved sending queue without requiring an open tab.

## Reviewer navigation and email reply

Replace the video marker below only after recording and checking the live flow.
Use this as a reply in the existing Google verification email thread after saving
and resubmitting the Cloud Console changes. Do not send the marker literally.
If reviewer access needs allowlisting, resolve it and adjust the access paragraph
before claiming the app is ready for testing.

```text
Hello Third Party Data Safety Team,

We have addressed the requested items for project mailloop-510915
(project number 842074495814) and updated our verification submission.

Privacy policy: https://mailloop.in/privacy
Google user data sharing disclosures:
https://mailloop.in/privacy#google-data-sharing
Sensitive data protection disclosures:
https://mailloop.in/privacy#data-protection

The policy identifies our service providers and selected recipients, the data
they process, and the purposes of sharing. It also describes encryption in
transit, encrypted stored refresh tokens, server-side credentials, account
access controls, and private resume storage.

Replacement demonstration video: [INSERT CHECKED VIDEO URL]
The video shows the full Google sign-in and consent flow with permissions
expanded, personalized individual sends with a selected PDF attachment, and
the resulting messages in the same sender account's Gmail Sent folder.

The current app requests openid, email, profile, and
https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.send only. It does not request Gmail
reading, mailbox modification, or deletion permissions. Gmail sending access
is required to send the messages users explicitly approve.

Reviewer access:
Mailloop uses Sign in with Google as its only login method. There is no
separate Mailloop username/password, paid subscription, credit-card
requirement, invitation, or app-level phone verification.

Testing instructions:
1. Visit https://mailloop.in/ and click "Get started with Google".
2. Sign in with your review Google account and grant Gmail sending permission.
3. In Settings, confirm Gmail sending is enabled. Optionally upload a small
   test PDF to demonstrate the resume attachment feature.
4. In Contacts, add a recipient address you control, a name, and a job role.
5. In Templates, create and save a template with a name, subject, and message.
6. In Compose, select that template and recipient, confirm the role and
   Personal Preview, and optionally select Attach Resume after uploading a PDF.
7. Click "Send to 1 recipient" and check History until the message shows Sent.
8. In the same sender Google account, open Gmail → Sent and inspect the
   resulting message and any selected attachment.

Please let us know if your reviewer account requires specific authorization
or if additional information is needed to complete testing.

Thank you,
Mailloop / Czar16
```
